LESSON: MUSICAL SOUNDS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Creating and Execution
Topic 1.2: Musical Sounds
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Musical Sounds, part of Creating and Execution in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How are sounds produced in the environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify sounds in their immediate environment for aural discrimination,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Musical Sounds in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. imitate sounds in their immediate environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Musical Sounds in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. sing songs that involve sounds from their immediate environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Musical Sounds in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. make body movements to imitate musical sounds,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Musical Sounds in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate imitating sounds in their immediate environment. ● Learners to critically listen to different sounds within the school environment. Safety precautions for all the learners should be observed with extra caution taken for learners with health conditions and those using mobility devices by ensuring that they move in a safe environment. ●Learners to watch or listen to recorded clips of various sounds of birds, animals and objects and identify the sounds they produce. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated when using digital devices to support learners who are sensitive to light. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication. How are sounds produced in the environment? 5 ●Learners to use flash cards or pictures of birds, animals or objects and take turns to imitate the sounds they produce. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication. ●Learners to interact with digital devices to record imitated sounds of birds, animals and objects. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted digital devices, alternative functional parts of the body, assistive technology or be supported. ● Learners to listen keenly to and sing back familiar songs sung to them on various sounds of birds, animals and objects. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech to hum or mime back familiar songs sung to them. 6 ●Learners to use appropriate costumes and props (coloured paper masks of birds, animals and object

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Musical Sounds together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: as the learner listens keenly to and sings back familiar songs sung to them.

● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner performs songs that involve various sounds of animals, birds and objects

accompanied with appropriate actions.

Values:
● Responsibility is promoted as the learner cares for flash cards or pictures of birds, animals or objects as they imitate the

various sounds.

● Respect is enhanced as the learner appreciates peers’ imitations of the identified sounds of birds, animals and objects.

7

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Safety and security is nurtured as the learner observes own and others' safety as they walk around the school

environment identifying various sounds of birds, animals and objects.

Link to other learning areas:

● English, Kiswahili and Indigenous Languages Activities as the learner uses language skills learnt to express self when

imitating the identified sounds of birds, animals and objects.

● Environmental Activities as the learner applies knowledge gained in Environmental Activities to role play, imitate and

identify sounds of various birds, animals and objects.

Suggested learning resources:

Open space, costumes and props, adapted digital devices, laptops, tablets, phones, computers, flash cards or pictures of

birds, animals or objects, audio /visual recordings of musical sounds, relevant virtual sites
